transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… work, mainly. I made a decision there that I shouldn’t have. I pushed an onboarding launch forward and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place.

At the time it felt like the right move—bold, necessary. Now I’m on leave, and people keep asking what I was thinking.
Around the time you made that decision at work, were you needing much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I mean, sleep was… not great, but I couldn’t tell you if it was much less than usual. I wasn’t tracking it.
Around that time, did you feel unusually powerful, important, or especially confident in your abilities?
I don’t know. I mean, I felt… sure of myself, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it powerful or important. It’s hard to say now.
Around that time, were you talking much more than usual?

Maybe. In meetings I did notice I’d… keep going longer than I normally would. Talking faster, jumping between things—employee engagement, layouts for the gallery space, retention metrics. People kind of had to interrupt me to get a word in.
Around that time, did you feel unusually cheerful or euphoric for no clear reason?

Yeah… maybe not “cheerful” exactly. For a few weeks I felt really alive, like I finally knew what I was doing and could show leadership what HR should be. But if someone pushed back—even on small edits or budget stuff—I’d get angry pretty fast.
During that time, did you find yourself taking on a lot more projects or activities than usual?

Yeah… I guess I did. I was trying to handle the HR redesign, reach out to gallery people, contact festival organizers, and sort out staff conflicts all at the same time. It felt like if I had an idea, I needed to move on it right then.
During that time, did you believe you had special abilities or a unique mission that other people would find unrealistic?
I don’t know… “special abilities” sounds like a lot. I thought I had good ideas, maybe that I could see what needed fixing better than people around me, but I wouldn’t say it was some unique mission.
During that time, were you able to function well on much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
I’m not sure. My sleep was… not great, but I don’t really know that I was functioning “well” on less. I wasn’t tracking it like that.
During that time, did you hear or see things that other people could not?
No… not that I can think of. I mean, I was pretty keyed up, but I don’t remember hearing or seeing things other people couldn’t.
During that period, did your behavior or mood cause serious problems in your life, like getting put on leave at work?

Yeah… I mean, yes. It got serious. The way I handled the launch and the arguments around it… work didn’t take that well. I’ve been put on administrative leave, and they don’t really trust me with the HR projects I was leading anymore.
About how long did that period of feeling unusually energized and driven last?
I’d say… about a month. It kind of started building when the new executive began pushing back on my onboarding redesign.
During that month, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?
I’m not really sure. My sleep was off, but I don’t know that I’d say I felt rested. It’s a little hard to judge.
Did this period of feeling unusually energized begin only after the conflict at work started?
I think it started around then, yeah. It’s been building for about a month, since that executive started pushing back on my onboarding redesign.
Were you hospitalized during that period?
No… I mean, not that I’d call hospitalized. I wasn’t admitted anywhere.
During that month, did other people say your behavior seemed clearly unlike your usual self?

A couple people did, yeah. They said I was… more intense than usual. I felt like I was finally seeing what needed to happen, but if someone questioned me, even over small things, I’d get pretty angry.
During that month, were you sleeping much less than usual without feeling tired the next day?
I’m not really sure. I mean, my sleep’s been a bit off, but I haven’t been tracking it or anything. I can’t say for sure.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know. I’ve had low stretches, sure, but… two weeks, most of the day every day? I’m not really sure I’d say that.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not sure. I’ve had times where I felt pretty low, but I don’t really know if it was nearly every day for two full weeks.
At any point in your life, have you had a two-week period when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like doing much, but I don’t know if it was almost everything for two weeks straight.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period when you felt unusually energized or driven like this?
I’m not sure. Maybe there were times I felt more keyed up or busy, but I don’t know if it was like this or really unusual.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes an approximately one-month period of abnormally increased energy/drive with pressured or excessive speech, racing/jumping ideas, increased goal-directed activity, irritability, and impaired judgment causing marked occupational consequences (administrative leave). Psychotic symptoms were denied and hospitalization did not occur, supporting mania without psychotic symptoms. Bipolar disorder remains a differential because prior episodes were not clearly established, and adjustment disorder/work-related problems were considered given onset around workplace conflict, but the syndrome is more consistent with a manic episode than a stress reaction alone.
